description: qyl-owned vocabulary, first-class next to the pinned upstream registries (qyl architecture, loop 1). scripts/generate.sh (merge_registries.py) merges this file into resolved-registry.json as the third source: a `sources` entry {source_registry: qyl, source_ref: qyl-registry.json, source_commit: SHA-256 of this file's bytes, schema_url: null, source_date_epoch: null} (qyl publishes no schema URL and has no upstream date), and every merged qyl row carries the same five provenance fields. Attributes join the catalog, vendor_models join the catalog too, metrics join metrics and groups with attribute references resolved against the merged catalog, local_attribute_values append qyl-local members to an upstream open enum (the only sanctioned way a qyl row touches an upstream row; each member carries a note saying the value is local to qyl and absent upstream, and the merge fails the moment upstream lands the same value so the local declaration is deleted), and scope_names / event_names / vendor_scope_names land at the root. `attributes` is the qyl.* namespace and nothing else: the merge refuses an attribute there that does not start with `qyl.`. A key outside qyl.* reaches the catalog only through a `vendor_models` entry, which names the library, its exact pinned version, the repository and tag the finding was read at, and the ActivitySources it emits on, and carries per attribute the file and line that sets it; there is no prefix allowlist. Both paths still refuse any attribute, metric, or metric group that shadows an upstream row. Attributes are qyl.* names the platform emits and the collector must recognize; vendor attributes are the keys a pinned third-party library emits on its own ActivitySource or Meter and that upstream semconv does not define, declared so the collector's registry-derived allowlist keeps them; scope_names are the ActivitySource/Meter names qyl constructs; vendor_scope_names are the ActivitySource names qyl subscribes to but does not own; event_names are qyl-owned Activity or DiagnosticSource event names. Every downstream projection (Roslyn generators, emit_analyzer_registry.py QYL0200/QYL0201 allowlists, the public registry stream) reads the merged file; emit_typespec_keys.py deliberately excludes qyl rows. Entries under qyl.mcp.* are the experimental staging namespace: deletion-targeted on every upstream registry bump that lands an equivalent.

attributes.brief: First dot-segment of the attribute key a collector measurement is about.
attributes.note: The value set is closed and is exactly the attribute namespaces present in the merged registry plus `other`: the collector clamps every value it records to this set, so an inbound payload carrying an unknown key cannot fork the series. merge_registries.py recomputes the set from the merged catalog on every generation and fails the merge when the two disagree, so a registry that gains a namespace cannot silently leave it unlisted.
